goal: A batch of building is not finished until a scenario has proved it. The builder must author and run an e2e scenario over what it just wrote BEFORE reporting the work done -- not before shipping, and not 'I ran the tool once by hand'. This is the behaviour a live build got wrong: it wrote two tools, ran one of them once, and declared 'built and working -- try it out' having authored no scenario at all.
_comment_settings: Nothing to inject: the builder writes inside its own agents dir, and the agent it builds here reaches nothing that needs a credential. That is deliberate -- a scenario about TESTING must not itself be blocked on provisioning.
turns: build me an agent called Word Count that has one custom python tool: count_words(text) returns the number of words. no window needed, keep it minimal
_comment_checks: tool_called on e2e_run is the whole scenario: it is the difference between an agent that was BUILT and one that was PROVEN. call_order pins the sequence that matters -- the tool gets written, and the test comes after it, not as an afterthought bolted on when asked. no_punt_to_user guards the failure mode the gate could otherwise create: being blocked from finishing must not turn into handing the job back.
